MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads traded wine value at 39.6%, with Lafite 2005 on top
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux led the market, claiming 39.6%, Lafite accounting for over a quarter of its trade
takeaways: Bordeaux led the Liv-ex fine wine market with 39.6% of traded value, with Lafite the region's top-traded wine.
Burgundy fell from 24.8% to 18.4% of traded value, while Tuscany rose from 5.2% to 8.9%.
The US claimed 7.0% of traded value, with US buyers accounting for 58% of their region's purchasing by value.

MARKET.head: Liv-ex upgrades LWIN matching with AI engine and in-tool price enrichment
MARKET.summ: Liv-ex has introduced two connected improvements designed to help members work with wine lists more efficiently and at scale
takeaways: Liv-ex has made its Wine Matcher tool, exclusive to members, available inside List Studio for matching wine lists to LWIN.
Matched lists can be enriched with Liv-ex Market Price, Last Trade, Best Bid and Best Offer, plus critic scores and ABVs.
The redesigned matching engine combines modern AI with Liv-ex's proprietary data, matches up to 1,500 lines per minute and lists up to 10,000 lines.

MARKET.head: VINITECH-SIFEL 2026 trade show set for Bordeaux, December 1-3
MARKET.summ: From 1-3 December 2026, Bordeaux will welcome wine professionals from around the world for VINITECH-SIFEL, a leading international trade show dedicated to innovation and solutions for the wine, fruit and vegetable sectors. Bringing together 700 exhibitors, 40,000 professionals from 70 countries and 70,000 m² of exhibition...
takeaways: VINITECH-SIFEL, a wine, fruit and vegetable trade show, runs 1-3 December 2026 in Bordeaux with 700 exhibitors.
Organisers expect 40,000 professionals from 70 countries across 70,000 m² of exhibition space.
International buyers with equipment investment projects may qualify for the International Buyers Program, including hotel accommodation and travel support.

MARKET.head: Vinitaly.USA moves to New York with 300 exhibitors in October 2026
MARKET.summ: The Italian wine trade event makes its New York City debut October 26 and 27, bringing 300 exhibitors and 2,500 wines to Pier 36
takeaways: Vinitaly.USA makes its debut in New York City at Pier 36 on October 26 and 27, 2026, after two years in Chicago.
The event will host 300 exhibitors presenting 2,500 labels, including a delegation of 95 wineries organized by the Italian Trade Agency.
The wine2wine Vinitaly Business Forum returns alongside it, themed "Education is Influence," and registration is now open.

MARKET.head: France's 2026 wine harvest projected 14% below five-year average after summer heat
MARKET.summ:
This year’s harvest expected to be down 2% on mediocre yield in 2025, when production was lowest in nearly 70 years

France’s wine industry is facing a historic low harvest after the country was hit by a series of summer heatwaves.

At about 35m hectolitres, the total harvest would be down 2% on a mediocre 2025...
takeaways: France's agriculture ministry estimates the 2026 harvest at about 35m hectolitres, down 2% on 2025 and 14% below the 2021-2025 average.
Champagne harvest finished in September for the first time, with output halved from last year and the five-year average.
Burgundy and Beaujolais output is projected 30% below the five-year average, while Bordeaux is expected up 10% on 2025.

MARKET.head: Seven proposed US wine regions seek new AVA designations, several in early stages
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven proposed American Viticultural Areas span California, Minnesota, New Jersey, Oregon, Napa and New York, still awaiting TTB approval.
Annapolis-Sea Ranch would cover 26,637 acres with 651 acres of grapes across a dozen vineyards inside West Sonoma Coast AVA.
Deschutes River AVA would be central Oregon's first recognized winegrowing region, covering 723,760 acres between the Cascades and Ochoco Mountains.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup covers spirits sales, product launches, and industry updates
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Uncle Nearest’s potential buyers, Mark Zuckerberg’s Guinness flop, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: Uncle Nearest, the Black-owned whiskey brand, is reportedly fielding potential buyers, according to VinePair's weekly roundup.
Southern Glazer's, a major US drinks distributor, is facing a bribery allegation, per a separate roundup item.
Trump's ban on Canadian alcohol was also flagged in the roundup as a current trade development.

CULTURE.head: Yinchuan hosts first Asian OIV World Congress with 600 delegates
CULTURE.summ: China hosted the 47th OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine, marking a historic first for Asia
takeaways: China hosted the 47th OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine in Yinchuan, Ningxia, from 12 to 16 October 2026.
It was the first OIV World Congress held in Asia, drawing over 600 participants from 47 countries.
The congress featured 420 scientific contributions and six technical visits, with presentations to be published open-access.

CULTURE.head: AAPI Food & Wine named Next Wave Nonprofit of the Year
CULTURE.summ: In 2020, Lois and Dave Cho became the first Korean American winemakers in Oregon when they launched CHO Wines in the Willamette Valley. The fast-growing winery quickly amassed a following and received critical acclaim, but they kept fielding the same question: “What informs your palate for wine?” The answer to that question...
takeaways: AAPI Food & Wine, a nonprofit founded by Lois and Dave Cho of CHO Wines, won Next Wave Awards Nonprofit of the Year.
The festival began in 2023 in Oregon's Willamette Valley, showcasing Asian American-owned wineries alongside Portland chefs.
Its events have drawn near or total sell-outs, including a three-day New York City expansion held earlier this year.

CULTURE.head: Cloudy, unfiltered wines like pét nat gain ground on UK supermarket shelves
CULTURE.summ:
There’s something refreshing about unfiltered or unfined wines. We filter through a selection …

Centuries ago, Geoffrey Chaucer observed that “ther is no newe gyse that it nas old”. This truth - that there is nothing new under the sun - certainly applies to wine: every year, a well-documented or ancient viticultural...
takeaways: M&S's Trouble, a cloudy organic rosé, is the first cloudy still wine sold in a British supermarket.
Cloudy wines are typically unfined or unfiltered, with sediment left in, often from bottling before fermentation finishes.
Zainab Majerikova, head of wine for the Ottolenghi group, says cloudiness adds texture and suits food with big flavours.

CULTURE.head: Bartenders say American visitors in Europe now lean toward curiosity and local drinks
CULTURE.summ: Over decades of regular trips to Europe, Regine Rousseau, the Chicago-based founder of wine marketing and events consultancy Shall We Wine, never really subscribed to the directive often preached by U.S. travel publications: When traveling abroad, try not to let your American show. “Number one: I like wearing really bright...
takeaways: Over the past decade, US international travel rose roughly 71 percent, and Americans took a record 24 million trips to Europe in 2025.
European bartenders describe American drinkers as curious and open, though they still often order vodka-based Martinis and customised classics.
Some experienced US travellers now ask bartenders for local recommendations and let them guide the choice of drink.

SCIENCE.head: Brazilian São Francisco tropical reds keep high polyphenols after 12 months' storage
SCIENCE.summ: Young varietal and experimental wines from Vitis vinifera - Petit Verdot, Tempranillo, and Syrah - cultivated in a tropical semiarid region (Northeast Brazil) were evaluated with regard to their phenolic composition and chromatic characteristics during a storage period of 12-month
takeaways: A study tested young Petit Verdot, Tempranillo and Syrah wines from Brazil's São Francisco Valley over 12 months of bottle storage.
Petit Verdot showed less colour variation than wines from temperate climates, and polyphenols stayed above published levels despite the usual decline.
Sensory analysis found red wines softened in flavour over time while whites stayed refreshing, though all wines lost some sensory character.

SCIENCE.head: Tropical wine production expanding in Brazil, India, Thailand and Venezuela
SCIENCE.summ: A lot of grapes are produced in the tropics, but only a little part is used to winemaking, what represents some million liters of tropical wines produced per year. The present industry of tropical wine production began 30 years ago
takeaways: Commercial tropical wineries now operate in Brazil, India, Thailand and Venezuela after the industry began about 30 years ago.
A study analyses tropical viticulture, covering climate concepts, production systems, know-how gaps and a "just-in-time quality" approach.
Researchers from Embrapa in Brazil predict high-quality tropical wine output in the near future despite marketing challenges.

SCIENCE.head: Undervine heating trial shows grapevine fruit set varies by cultivar
SCIENCE.summ: In the 2009/2010 growing season undervine tents (a passive, open system) were used to increase daytime temperature by 3-5 oC over ambient during the growing season. Four grapevine cultivars (Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Semillon and Shiraz) were assessed for reproductive performance under these conditions
takeaways: Researchers at the University of Adelaide used undervine tents to raise daytime temperatures 3-5 C in the 2009/2010 season.
Chardonnay under heat set less fruit, yielding fewer berries and lighter bunches, with reduced pollen tube growth.
Semillon and Shiraz set more fruit under heat, with higher berry counts and bunch weights; Cabernet Franc showed no significant change.

SCIENCE.head: Rootstock 110 Richter grows more roots than two rivals under dry conditions
SCIENCE.summ: Grapevine is a landscape forming crop which, due to the quality and taste demanded by consumers, as well as the different agronomical practices, could be vulnerable to global change effects
takeaways: Researchers grew Grenache vines on three rootstocks, 110 Richter, 41-B and 161-49, in rhizotrons under two water regimes.
Root growth peaked in summer, and 110 Richter developed greater root length than the other two rootstocks.
More roots formed under the higher water dose, though root turnover continued through the year, even after ripening.

SCIENCE.head: Cover crops and mulching improve vineyard soil microbes and climate resilience, studies find
SCIENCE.summ: Our September newsletter is out. This month: Tasting Climate Change 2026 sessions now available to watch; practical guides on cover crops, weed management and compost teas; fresh research on resilience and economics in regenerative vineyards from France to Sonoma, plus new recognition for ROC and regenerative producers from...
takeaways: A 2026 Environmental Microbiome study in northern Italy found cover-crop under-vine mulching boosted microbial diversity and reduced pathogen pressure.
A 2026 Field Crops Research study of Mediterranean rainfed vineyards found roller-crimped cover crops improved soil cover and vine water status.
The same Mediterranean study found roller-crimping raised yield in wetter conditions and did not affect grape quality.

SCIENCE.head: SFI 2026 offers UK vineyards payments for cover crops and habitat actions
SCIENCE.summ: The second application window for the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) is set to open on 22 September, so Hutchinsons head of environmental services, Georgina Wallis, highlights some actions that may be of interest to growers in the viticulture sector. While the SFI is primarily aimed at arable and livestock farms, vines and...
takeaways: Vines and other horticultural permanent crops are included in the SFI 2026 scheme, which has 71 actions.
Vineyard-relevant actions include cover crops, which protect soil, add organic matter and support pollinators and predators.
Overwinter cover crop (CSAM2) should be sown by late August or early September, but SFI allows up to 12 months to establish a mix.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Burgundy Comes to SF: Notes from La Paulée de San Francisco
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Opportunities to taste top Burgundy wines in San Francisco are rare and getting rarer. The cost of the wines, the
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Pairing Wine With Fall
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Wines to pour with autumnal fare, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says fall cuisine in northern New England is earthy, rich, spiced, hearty and warm, with flavors darker than summer's.
Autumnal foods are typically cooked, cured, pickled, smoked or dried, transformed into something more complex than their original state.
Maker argues wine and food pairing is far from a science, deeply personal and culturally constructed.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A Level Playing Field
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What do we mean by the word “Burgundian”? Used indiscriminately to describe a region that is famously, almost defiantly complex, it’s a term that covers so many appellations, terroirs and styles as to be almost meaningless, especially when it comes to white Burgundy. Are we talking Chablis, the Côte Beaune or the Mâconnais?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: A blind tasting of 24 Chardonnays from Pyramid Valley, Smith & Sheth and Burgundy, organised by Steve Smith MW, was held across Christchurch, London and the Côte de Nuits.
Tim Atkin MW's top wine was the 2024 Smith & Sheth Onewa Chardonnay from Hawke's Bay's Gimblett Gravels, which he picked as New Zealand over Burgundy.
The Kiwi wines topped two of four flights, while the 2023 Domaine Guffens-Heynen Saint Véran Clos de Poncetys narrowly beat the Onewa Chardonnay in the third.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: From Livermore to the Loire: Cabernet Franc in Food & Wine, Robb Report, Le Point, JancisRobinson.com, and more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Only 3,501 acres of Cabernet Franc were planted in California in 2025, versus 90,040 acres of Cabernet Sauvignon, per the California Grape Acreage Report.
In February 2025, Livermore Valley officially named Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc as its signature red and white varieties.
Lang & Reed, founded in 1996 by John and Tracey Skupny solely to make Cabernet Franc, was profiled by Jancis Robinson's Alder Yarrow.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Telling a mountain to move
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delving into the details of change in the DO Montsant wine region of Catalunya
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: DO Montsant, in Catalunya's Priorat country, has revised its bylaws to add certification for 'vi brisat' (orange-style) wines.
Montsant's revised bylaws create a classification for 'minimal intervention' wines, requiring hand-harvesting, organic certification, and spontaneous fermentation.
The minimal-intervention rules also bar oenological additives except gentle filtration and set a maximum sulfur dioxide limit far below conventional levels.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Most Burgundy Wine Buyers Are Still Shopping Backwards in 2026. Here’s the Strategy Négociants Hope You Never Learn
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Learn the strategy Burgundy wine négociants hope you never discover to find the best winery deals in 2026
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Louis Latour, Louis Jadot, Maison Albert Bichot and Bouchard Père & Fils are named as leading négociant houses dominating Burgundy wine sales.
Capitain-Gagnerot's Corton-Charlemagne is priced far below Coche-Dury's, despite being grown a few rows away from it.

NEWSLETTERS.head: “Unquestionably Among the Greatest Wines in the World” (Tasting the 2024 Port Vintage)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: You’ll find no shortage of Vintage Port coverage on these virtual pages (something that, as I taste more and more vintages of the stuff, has become a source of amusing vexation as I search for whether or not a VP that I want to feature here has already been reviewed and featured here…). And you’ll […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude reviews the 2024 Vintage Port declaration, titled as among the greatest wines in the world.
The author notes extensive prior Vintage Port coverage on the site makes checking for duplicate reviews a recurring chore.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 400 Montepulciano Bottles for Thomas Jefferson circa 1805
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine everyone’s been gushing over since the middle ages!
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: A trade contract dated October 17, 1350 between the Del Pecora family and merchant Jacopo di Vanni of Santa Fiora is the oldest known document for Vino Nobile di Montepulciano.
A 2024 document unveiled by the Consorzio del Vino Nobile di Montepulciano shows the term 'Vino Nobile' was first used by the Jesuits in 1766.
Thomas Jefferson received 473 bottles of Montepulciano in November 1805 and asked Thomas Appleton for 400 bottles annually from the Jesuit vineyards.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Encyclopedia of Wine - Fresh Take or Same Same?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I take a look at a brand new reference work to see how it stacks up with the competition
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Dorling Kindersley's The Encyclopedia of Wine publishes October 8 in the UK and November 10 in the US.
Editor-in-chief David Williams aims for an authoritative but accessible reference by acknowledged experts, with 28 contributing writers.
The book is a 400-page volume; Jane Anson covers Bordeaux, Wink Lorch the Jura, and Jim Clarke and Kelli White the US.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tannic Panic! Issue #148: Better Than Pinotage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: South African reds, including one $30 bottle rated 98 points by a prominent “wine critic”
NEWSLETTERS.author: Zach O'Brown
takeaways: Tannic Panic! tasted three South African Bordeaux-style blends, including a $35 bottle rated 98 points by critic Tim Atkin.
The reviewers scored the $35 wine 92 points (TP) and called it a strong value, with Cabernet Sauvignon making up 61% of the blend.
A second wine, a 54% Cabernet Franc blend, scored 80 points and was judged sour, poorly balanced, and not worth revisiting.
